items.text: Varying the space
$f\colon X\to Y$ continuous; $F$ a sheaf on $X$, $G$ a sheaf on $Y$.
$f$-homomorphisms $G\to F$
Arrows go against $f$. For $f=\mathrm{id}$: ordinary homomorphisms.
Data: for each pair of open sets $U\subset X$, $V\subset Y$ with $f(U)\subset V$,
u_{U,V}\colon G(V)\longrightarrow F(U)
compatible with restrictions ($U'\subset U$, $V'\subset V$):
\begin{CD} G(V) @>{u_{U,V}}>> F(U)\\ @VVV @VVV\\ G(V') @>{u_{U',V'}}>> F(U') \end{CD}
Largest $U$ over $V$ is $f^{-1}(V)$: all is determined by
u_V\colon G(V)\longrightarrow F\bigl(f^{-1}(V)\bigr)
Condition: for $V'\subset V$ the squares commute.
Same for presheaves. Reformulate with the functor of inverse image of opens:
\mathcal O(f)\colon\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X,\qquad V\mapsto f^{-1}(V)\quad\text{(commutes with unions)}
Direct image
(f_*F)(V)=F\bigl(f^{-1}(V)\bigr),\qquad f_*F=F\circ\mathcal O(f)^{\circ}
\operatorname{Hom}_f(G,F)\;=\;\operatorname{Hom}_Y(G,\,f_*F)
On presheaves $f_*$ commutes with all direct and inverse limits (composition of functors).
Claim: $f_*$ sends sheaves to sheaves.
For a covering $V=\bigcup V_i$ the sheaf diagram of $f_*F$ is
F(f^{-1}V)\to\prod_i F(f^{-1}V_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}F(f^{-1}V_{ij})
f^{-1}V=\bigcup_i f^{-1}V_i,\qquad f^{-1}(V_i\cap V_j)=f^{-1}V_i\cap f^{-1}V_j
It is the sheaf diagram of $F$ for the covering of $f^{-1}(V)$: exact.
On sheaves $f_*$ commutes with all inverse limits (those of sheaves are those of presheaves).
But not with direct limits: sums, initial object, epimorphisms.
Test case: $Y=\mathrm{pt}$, $\operatorname{Top}(\mathrm{pt})=\mathbf{Sets}$.
f_*F=\Gamma(X,F)=F(X)
Empty sheaf goes to the empty set only if $X\neq\varnothing$; sums are not preserved.
Only inverse limits: typical of a right adjoint. So look for a left adjoint.
Inverse image
For a sheaf $G$ on $Y$: a sheaf $f^*G$ on $X$ with an $f$-morphism $G\to f^*G$, universal.
\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^*G,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_f(G,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_Y(G,f_*F)\qquad f^*\dashv f_*
For presheaves too, but the two solutions differ:
f^*G=\widetilde{\,f^*_{\mathrm{pr}}G\,}\quad\text{(associated sheaf)}
General nonsense: any functor $\alpha\colon\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$ gives $\alpha^{\circ}\colon\hat{\mathcal O}_X\to\hat{\mathcal O}_Y$ with adjoints on both sides.
Reference: SGA 4, vol. 1 (exposé I or II).
Then: $\operatorname{Hom}(f^*_{\mathrm{pr}}G,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_f(G,F)$ and maps from a presheaf to a sheaf factor through the associated sheaf.
Properties: $f^*$ commutes with all direct limits (left adjoint), as $f_*$ with inverse ones.
f^*\ \text{left exact: commutes with finite products, final object, kernels}
Not from adjointness alone: needs the other picture.
Inverse image via étale spaces
Direct image: functors on opens are convenient; inverse image: étale spaces.
$G\to Y$ étale. Base change = fibre product:
f^*G=X\times_Y G=\{(x,g): f(x)=\pi(g)\}\subset X\times G
With the induced product topology it is a fibre product of spaces.
$G=\bigcup G_i$, each $G_i\hookrightarrow Y$ open: the preimages are $f^{-1}(\text{open})$, homeomorphic to opens of $X$. Hence étale over $X$.
Étale is stable under base change.
Claim (easy check): this agrees with the adjoint $f^*$ of sheaves.
Left exactness: base change commutes with finite inverse limits, and so does their computation in étale spaces.
Fibres: the fibre of $X\times_Y G$ at $x$ is the fibre of $G$ at $f(x)$.
(X\times_Y G)_x\simeq G_{f(x)}
Stalks of étale spaces = stalks of sheaves. Left exactness can be checked on stalks.
Next time
All interesting topological properties of $X$ — homological, homotopical, finer — are carried by the category $\operatorname{Top}(X)$.
For usual spaces, $X$ can be recovered from this category.
Continuous maps $\leftrightarrow$ functors $f^*$, $f_*$. Then: forget the space, keep the category of sheaves — generalised topological spaces.
